questions.q: **Directions (Q.1-4):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a straight row facing north. B sits third from the left end. A sits immediately to the right of B. Only two persons sit between A and E. C sits at one of the extreme ends. D sits immediately to the left of E. G sits immediately to the right of C. Who sits exactly in the middle of the row?
questions.solution: B is 3rd from left, A immediately right of B, so B-3, A-4. Two persons between A and E puts E at seat 1 or 7; but D sits immediately left of E, so E = 7 and D = 6. C is at an extreme end, hence seat 1, and G immediately right of C = seat 2. F takes the remaining seat 5. Final row (left to right): C-G-B-A-F-D-E. Seat 4 (the middle of 7) is occupied by **A**. **Answer: A**
questions.shortcut: Fix the anchored pair (B-3, A-4) first; the rest falls out in two moves.

questions.q: **Directions (Q.1-4):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a straight row facing north. B sits third from the left end. A sits immediately to the right of B. Only two persons sit between A and E. C sits at one of the extreme ends. D sits immediately to the left of E. G sits immediately to the right of C. How many persons sit between F and G?
questions.solution: CGBAFDE: F is 5th and G is 2nd, with B and A between them - two persons. **Answer: Two**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.1-4):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a straight row facing north. G sits immediately to the right of C. Who sits immediately to the left of D?
questions.solution: CGBAFDE: D is 6th, so the person immediately to his left (5th seat) is **F**. **Answer: F**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.1-4):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a straight row facing north. B sits third from the left end. A sits immediately to the right of B. Only two persons sit between A and E. C sits at one of the extreme ends. D sits immediately to the left of E. G sits immediately to the right of C. Which of the following pairs sits at the extreme ends of the row?
questions.solution: CGBAFDE: seat 1 = C and seat 7 = E. **Answer: C, E**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.5-8):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Five persons P, Q, R, S and T live on five different floors of a building; the ground floor is numbered 1 and the topmost floor is numbered 5. R lives on an even-numbered floor. Only two persons live between R and S. P lives immediately above Q. T does not live on the topmost floor. Q does not live on the ground floor. Who lives on floor number 4?
questions.solution: R is on floor 2 or 4, and two persons between R and S means S = R +/- 3, so (R, S) = (2, 5) or (4, 1). If (4, 1), the free floors {2, 3, 5} cannot hold P immediately above Q without putting T on floor 5 - not allowed. Hence R = 2, S = 5, and from the free floors {1, 3, 4}: P immediately above Q gives Q = 3, P = 4, leaving T = 1 (not topmost, as required). **Answer: P**
questions.shortcut: Test the two cases for R (2 or 4); one dies immediately on the P-above-Q rule.

questions.q: **Directions (Q.5-8):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Five persons P, Q, R, S and T live on five different floors of a building; the ground floor is numbered 1 and the topmost floor is numbered 5. R lives on an even-numbered floor. Only two persons live between R and S. P lives immediately above Q. T does not live on the topmost floor. Q does not live on the ground floor. Who lives immediately below S?
questions.solution: R is on floor 2 or 4, and two persons between R and S means S = R +/- 3, so (R, S) = (2, 5) or (4, 1). If (4, 1), the free floors {2, 3, 5} cannot hold P immediately above Q without putting T on floor 5 - not allowed. Hence R = 2, S = 5, and from the free floors {1, 3, 4}: P immediately above Q gives Q = 3, P = 4, leaving T = 1 (not topmost, as required). S is on floor 5, so floor 4, immediately below S, has **P**. **Answer: P**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.5-8):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Five persons P, Q, R, S and T live on five different floors of a building; the ground floor is numbered 1 and the topmost floor is numbered 5. R lives on an even-numbered floor. Only two persons live between R and S. P lives immediately above Q. T does not live on the topmost floor. Q does not live on the ground floor. How many persons live between T and Q?
questions.solution: R is on floor 2 or 4, and two persons between R and S means S = R +/- 3, so (R, S) = (2, 5) or (4, 1). If (4, 1), the free floors {2, 3, 5} cannot hold P immediately above Q without putting T on floor 5 - not allowed. Hence R = 2, S = 5, and from the free floors {1, 3, 4}: P immediately above Q gives Q = 3, P = 4, leaving T = 1 (not topmost, as required). T = 1 and Q = 3, with only R on floor 2 between them - one person. **Answer: One**

Only two persons live between R and S. P lives immediately above Q. T does not live on the topmost floor. Q does not live on the ground floor. Which of the following floor-person combinations is correct?
questions.solution: R is on floor 2 or 4, and two persons between R and S means S = R +/- 3, so (R, S) = (2, 5) or (4, 1). If (4, 1), the free floors {2, 3, 5} cannot hold P immediately above Q without putting T on floor 5 - not allowed. Hence R = 2, S = 5, and from the free floors {1, 3, 4}: P immediately above Q gives Q = 3, P = 4, leaving T = 1 (not topmost, as required). Checking the options, only Floor 3 - Q matches (T(1), R(2), Q(3), P(4), S(5)). **Answer: Floor 3 - Q**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.9-12):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Five persons J, K, L, M and N attend interviews on five different days of the same week, from Monday to Friday, one person per day. L attends immediately after K. M attends on Wednesday. J attends before N. J does not attend on Monday. Who attends the interview on Tuesday?
questions.solution: M is fixed on Wednesday. L immediately after K leaves pairs (Mon-Tue) or (Thu-Fri) for (K, L). If (K, L) = (Thu, Fri), then J and N must take Monday and Tuesday, but J cannot be on Monday and must precede N - impossible. So K = Monday, L = Tuesday, and the remaining Thursday-Friday go to J before N: J = Thursday, N = Friday. **Answer: L**
questions.shortcut: Anchor M on Wednesday, then test the only two slots for the K-L pair.

questions.q: **Directions (Q.9-12):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Five persons J, K, L, M and N attend interviews on five different days of the same week, from Monday to Friday, one person per day. L attends immediately after K. M attends on Wednesday. J attends before N. J does not attend on Monday. On which day does N attend the interview?
questions.solution: M is fixed on Wednesday. L immediately after K leaves pairs (Mon-Tue) or (Thu-Fri) for (K, L). If (K, L) = (Thu, Fri), then J and N must take Monday and Tuesday, but J cannot be on Monday and must precede N - impossible. So K = Monday, L = Tuesday, and the remaining Thursday-Friday go to J before N: J = Thursday, N = Friday. **Answer: Friday**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.9-12):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Five persons J, K, L, M and N attend interviews on five different days of the same week, from Monday to Friday, one person per day. L attends immediately after K. M attends on Wednesday. J attends before N. J does not attend on Monday. How many persons attend between K and M?
questions.solution: M is fixed on Wednesday. L immediately after K leaves pairs (Mon-Tue) or (Thu-Fri) for (K, L). If (K, L) = (Thu, Fri), then J and N must take Monday and Tuesday, but J cannot be on Monday and must precede N - impossible. So K = Monday, L = Tuesday, and the remaining Thursday-Friday go to J before N: J = Thursday, N = Friday. K is on Monday and M on Wednesday, with only L (Tuesday) between - one person. **Answer: One**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.9-12):** Study the following information carefully and answer the questions. Five persons J, K, L, M and N attend interviews on five different days of the same week, from Monday to Friday, one person per day. L attends immediately after K. M attends on Wednesday. J attends before N. J does not attend on Monday. Who attends the interview immediately before J?
questions.solution: M is fixed on Wednesday. L immediately after K leaves pairs (Mon-Tue) or (Thu-Fri) for (K, L). If (K, L) = (Thu, Fri), then J and N must take Monday and Tuesday, but J cannot be on Monday and must precede N - impossible. So K = Monday, L = Tuesday, and the remaining Thursday-Friday go to J before N: J = Thursday, N = Friday. J is on Thursday; the previous day (Wednesday) is **M**. **Answer: M**

questions.q: Statements: All pens are books. All books are copies. Conclusions: I. All pens are copies. II. Some copies are pens. Give answer -
questions.solution: Pens sit inside books, which sit inside copies, so all pens are copies (I follows). Since pens exist and all pens are copies, some copies are definitely pens (II follows). **Answer: Both conclusions follow**

questions.q: Statements: Some dogs are cats. No cat is a rat. Conclusions: I. Some dogs are not rats. II. All dogs are rats. Give answer -
questions.solution: The dogs that are cats cannot be rats (no cat is a rat), so some dogs are definitely not rats - I follows. II is the opposite extreme and is not forced. **Answer: Only conclusion I follows**

questions.q: Statements: Some cups are plates. No plate is a bowl. Conclusions: I. Some cups are bowls. II. No cup is a bowl. Give answer -
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: I and II form a complementary pair - for the cups and bowls, exactly one of 'some are' or 'none are' must be true. Neither is definite from the statements, but one of them must hold. **Answer: Either conclusion I or II follows**

questions.q: Statements: All keys are locks. Some locks are doors. Conclusions: I. Some keys are doors. II. Some doors are locks. Give answer -
questions.solution: 'Some locks are doors' may involve locks outside the keys, so I is not certain. II is a valid conversion of 'some locks are doors' (some doors are locks). **Answer: Only conclusion II follows**

questions.q: Statements: A > B $\geq$ C = D. Conclusions: I. A > D  II. C < A Give answer -
questions.solution: A > B $\geq$ C = D chains to A > D, so I follows. Also A > B $\geq$ C gives C < A, so II follows. **Answer: Both conclusions follow**
questions.shortcut: Chain the symbols in one direction; a mix of > with = keeps strict inequality.

questions.q: Statements: P $\leq$ Q < R; R $\geq$ S > T. Conclusions: I. P < R  II. S < Q Give answer -
questions.solution: P $\leq$ Q < R gives P < R, so I follows. Q and S are connected only through R, which points the same way for both - no definite relation, so II fails. **Answer: Only conclusion I follows**
questions.shortcut: When two branches meet at a common point via opposite signs, no conclusion is possible between the branch ends.

questions.q: Statements: X $\geq$ Y = Z; Z > W. Conclusions: I. X = W  II. W < Y Give answer -
questions.solution: Y = Z > W gives W < Y, so II follows. X $\geq$ Y only bounds X from below; X = W is not forced. **Answer: Only conclusion II follows**

questions.q: Statements: A $\geq$ B > C; C $\leq$ D. Conclusions: I. A > D  II. A $\leq$ D Give answer -
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: A and D are linked only through C, on which the signs diverge (B > C and C $\leq$ D), so neither I nor II is definite. But 'A > D' and 'A $\leq$ D' together cover every possibility, so one of them must be true. **Answer: Either conclusion I or II follows**
questions.shortcut: Complementary pair: conclusions of the form 'X > Y' and 'X $\leq$ Y' always yield either-or.

questions.q: In a certain code language, TEA is written as VGC. How will CUP be written in that code?
questions.solution: Each letter moves 2 places ahead: T->V, E->G, A->C. So C->E, U->W, P->R: **EWR**. **Answer: EWR**
questions.shortcut: Compare letter positions of the pair to find a constant shift, then apply it.

questions.q: In a certain code, WATER is coded as YCVGT. How will LAND be coded in the same language?
questions.solution: Every letter is shifted +2: W->Y, A->C, T->V, E->G, R->T. LAND becomes N->N+2? no: L->N, A->C, N->P, D->F = **NCPF**. **Answer: NCPF**

questions.q: In a certain code language, 'she is nice' is coded as 'ta pa ra', 'nice work done' is coded as 'ra ka na', and 'she did work' is coded as 'pa ja na'. What is the code for 'work'?
questions.solution: 'work' appears in the second and third sentences; their codes share exactly one word: 'na' (ra, ka with 'nice'; pa, ja with 'she'). So work = **na**. **Answer: na**
questions.shortcut: Find the word common to two sentences; its code is the code common to those two coded lines.

questions.q: If DELHI is coded as EFMIJ, how will MUMBAI be coded?
questions.solution: Each letter is shifted +1: D->E, E->F, L->M, H->I, I->J. So M->N, U->V, M->N, B->C, A->B, I->J = **NVNCBJ**. **Answer: NVNCBJ**

questions.q: If each letter is given a value equal to its position in the English alphabet (A = 1, B = 2, ...), and the code of a word is the sum of the values of its letters, then CAB is coded as 6. What will be the code of BEAD?
Pointing to a photograph, Ravi said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl in the photograph related to Ravi?
questions.solution: Grandfather's only son = Ravi's father. The daughter of Ravi's father is Ravi's **sister**. **Answer: Sister**
questions.group: Break the chain person by person: 'only son' collapses the grandfather branch to the father.

questions.q: A is the brother of B. C is the mother of A. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.solution: C is A's mother and D is C's father, so D is A's maternal grandfather. Therefore A is D's **grandson**. **Answer: Grandson**

questions.q: A man walks 5 km towards the north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: Path: 5 km north, then right (east) 3 km, then right (south) 5 km. The north-south walks (5 north + 5 south) cancel, leaving 3 km **East** of the start. **Answer: 3 km East**
questions.group: Track coordinates; equal distances in opposite directions cancel completely.

questions.q: Ravi walks 4 km towards the south, turns left and walks 6 km, then turns left again and walks 4 km. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: He walks 4 km south, turns left (now facing east) and walks 6 km, then turns left again (now facing north) and walks 4 km. The 4 km south and 4 km north legs cancel, leaving him exactly **6 km** from the start. **Answer: 6 km**
questions.group: Opposite equal legs cancel; only the middle leg survives.

questions.q: In a class, Amit ranks 12th from the top and 28th from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution: Total = (rank from top) + (rank from bottom) - 1 = 12 + 28 - 1 = **39** (Amit is counted twice). **Answer: 39**
questions.shortcut: Rank sums double-count the person; subtract 1.

questions.q: Ram is taller than Shyam but shorter than Mohan. Sohan is taller than Mohan. Rakesh is shorter than Shyam. Who is the tallest among them?
questions.solution: Chain: Sohan > Mohan > Ram > Shyam > Rakesh. The tallest is **Sohan**. **Answer: Sohan**
questions.shortcut: Arrange all comparisons into one descending chain before answering.

questions.q: In a row of 40 students, Rahul is 11th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.solution: Position from right = Total - position from left + 1 = 40 - 11 + 1 = **30**. **Answer: 30**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.33-35):** Study the following series carefully and answer the questions.  3 % K 7 @ M 2 T & 9 D # 4 W P 6 $ 8 Z * 5  How many symbols are immediately preceded by a number in the series?
questions.solution: Symbols: %, @, &, #, \$, *. Of these, % (after 3), @ (after 7) and \$ (after 6) are preceded by numbers, while &, # and * follow letters K, D and Z. So **three**. **Answer: Three**
questions.shortcut: List the symbols first, then walk left of each one.

questions.q: **Directions (Q.33-35):** Study the following series carefully and answer the questions.  3 % K 7 @ M 2 T & 9 D # 4 W P 6 $ 8 Z * 5  Which element is exactly in the middle of the series?
questions.solution: The series has 21 elements, so the middle is the 11th element, which is **D**. **Answer: D**

questions.q: **Directions (Q.33-35):** Study the following series carefully and answer the questions.  3 % K 7 @ M 2 T & 9 D # 4 W P 6 $ 8 Z * 5  If all the numbers are removed from the series, which element will be ninth from the left end?
questions.solution: After removing 3, 7, 2, 9, 4, 6, 8, 5 the series is: % K @ M T & D # W P $ Z * (13 elements). The 9th element is **W**. **Answer: W**
questions.shortcut: Rewrite the stripped series before counting; counting on the original invites slips.
